requirements.notes: Context holds locale ('en'|'ua') + setLocale + t(); LanguageProvider memoizes t on [locale] so a setLocale call re-renders every consumer live; LanguageToggle calls setLocale. The t()/translator core IS automated (createTranslator tests), but the React live re-render and context wiring are NOT covered by an automated test — the repo has no React/DOM test runner (ADR-0001). Live-switch behavior is verified by tsc + eslint (components/ clean) + build + the manual plan (test-plans/i18n.md TC-1/TC-3). No open reviewer findings on this ID.

evidence: lib/i18n.test.ts::"EN and UA dictionaries have the identical key set"
lib/i18n.test.ts::"every dictionary value is a non-empty string"
lib/i18n.test.ts::"UA values differ from EN for translated prose (not a copy-paste stub)"
requirements.notes: Two flat JSON dictionaries (en.json / ua.json, 75 keys each) with an asserted identical key set (missingKeys both directions == []); all values non-empty strings; sampled prose keys genuinely differ. t() is the single resolution path. TranslationKey is derived from the EN dictionary so downstream call sites get compile-time key checking (CR-001, resolved). SC-001 (resolved): the toggle's group aria-label is now sourced via t('language'), so it too resolves through the dictionary. Whether *every* user-facing string in downstream components actually routes through t() is a per-consumer property verified as those components ship — pinned here only for the strings this change owns.

evidence: lib/i18n.test.ts::"CALC_LABELS are the fixed module labels"
lib/i18n.test.ts::"calculation labels are NOT dictionary keys or translated values"
requirements.notes: Calc labels (¼M, ½M, M, 1.5M, 2M, 3M, 4M) are isolated in the CALC_LABELS constant, not dictionary keys and not dictionary values. The never-translate test asserts, for both en and ua, that no label appears as a key or a value — so a label cannot become locale-dependent. Matches DESIGN §11 never-translate rule. No open findings.
